docs.t: Departure Briefing complete. What does it trigger?
docs.x: Departure Briefing complete. What does it trigger? Cockpit Preparation Checklist Checklist trigger: Departure briefing completed.

docs.t: Push/start clearance received. What does it trigger?
docs.x: Push/start clearance received. What does it trigger? Before Start flow, then Before Start Checklist Checklist trigger: ‐ Pushback clearance or start clearance received, and ‐ Before Start flow pattern completed.

docs.t: Engines started. What event starts the After Start flow?
docs.x: Engines started. What event starts the After Start flow? PF sets the ENG START selector to NORM The PF sets the ENG START selector to NORM to permit normal pack operation. At this time, the After Start flow pattern begins.

docs.t: What triggers the After Start Checklist?
docs.x: What triggers the After Start Checklist? Hand signal (salute) from the ground personnel Checklist trigger: On hand signal (salute) from the ground personnel.

docs.t: During taxi: what has to happen before the Taxi flow starts?
docs.x: During taxi: what has to happen before the Taxi flow starts? Brake check, flight control check, ATC clearance confirmed, then AFS/Flight Instruments checked. That check is the flow trigger. Review the ATC clearance before checking the AFS/Flight Instruments

docs.t: What triggers the Taxi Checklist?
docs.x: What triggers the Taxi Checklist? T.O CONFIG pb pressed and Takeoff Advisory PA complete Checklist trigger: ‐ T.O. CONFIG pb pressed, and ‐ Takeoff Advisory PA complete (if applicable).

docs.t: Takeoff PA: who, how far ahead, and the words?
docs.x: Takeoff PA: who, how far ahead, and the words? PM, no less than two minutes prior to takeoff: [FLIGHT ATTENDANTS SHOULD NOW] BE SEATED FOR TAKEOFF Advise the cabin that takeoff is imminent. On Pax aircraft, The PM will make the Takeoff PA no less than two minutes prior to takeoff stating "[FLIGHT ATTENDANTS SHOULD NOW] BE SEATED FOR TAKEOFF".

docs.t: Line-up clearance received. What does it trigger?
docs.x: Line-up clearance received. What does it trigger? Line-Up flow, then Line-Up Checklist Checklist trigger: ‐ Line-up clearance received ‐ Line-Up flow pattern completed.

docs.t: Takeoff clearance received. The two light switches?
After takeoff: what triggers the Acceleration flow, and is there a checklist behind it?
docs.x: After takeoff: what triggers the Acceleration flow, and is there a checklist behind it? Selection of flaps 0 (at S speed). No checklist: the A330 has no After Takeoff checklist. ABOVE ACCELERATION ALTITUDE (OR ONCE IN CLIMB PHASE) L2 The following procedure ensures that the aircraft is correctly accelerating toward climb speed.

docs.t: Climbing through 10,000 ft MSL. Who selects which EFIS option?
docs.x: Climbing through 10,000 ft MSL. Who selects which EFIS option? PF selects CSTR, PM selects ARPT EFIS Option: The PF will select CSTR The PM will select ARPT

docs.t: Cabin preparation PA: who, when, and the words?
docs.x: Cabin preparation PA: who, when, and the words? PM, no later than about 18,000 ft MSL (near T/D on short legs, or when Early Sit is used): [Flight Attendants], please prepare the cabin for arrival and be seated for landing. "[Flight Attendants], please prepare the cabin for arrival and be seated for landing."

docs.t: Descending through 10,000 ft AAL. The flow?
docs.x: Descending through 10,000 ft AAL. The flow? LAND ON, SEAT BELTS ON, NO SMOKING cycle (PM); EFIS CSTR both sides; LS pb as required (PF-PM); NAVAIDS check (PF); ENG START selector as required (PM). Then the Approach Checklist once baro is set. L2 Select CSTR on both sides.

docs.t: What triggers the Approach Checklist?
docs.x: What triggers the Approach Checklist? Below 10,000 ft AAL and barometric reference set (or after the approach briefing when staying in the terminal area) Checklist trigger: ‐ Below 10 000 ft AAL and barometric reference set, or ‐ After the approach briefing is completed, for the case when not leaving the terminal area or climbing above 10 000 ft AAL (Case of an Air Turn Back or Traffic Pattern or Go Around)

docs.t: Flaps at 2. What comes next, and who does it?
Cleared for approach, then cleared to land: the exterior lights?
docs.x: Cleared for approach, then cleared to land: the exterior lights? Cleared for approach: NOSE TAXI, RWY TURN OFF ON. Cleared to land: NOSE T.O. All PM. docs.t: What triggers the Landing Checklist?
docs.x: What triggers the Landing Checklist? LDG CONF set (landing flaps selected, LDG MEMO checked no blue) Checklist trigger: LDG CONF set.

docs.t: Runway vacated. First action, and what does it trigger?
docs.x: Runway vacated. First action, and what does it trigger? PF disarms GND SPLRS. That starts the After Landing flow, then the After Landing Checklist. GND SPLRS............<wbr>............<wbr>............<wbr>............<wbr>............<wbr>............<wbr>............<wbr>..........DISARM PF

docs.t: At the gate: how long before the ENG MASTER levers come off, and who?
docs.x: At the gate: how long before the ENG MASTER levers come off, and who? No less than 1 min after high thrust operations; PF sets all ENG MASTER levers OFF The flight crew must operate the engines at or near idle thrust for a cooling period of 1 min before engine shutdown, in order to thermally stabilize the engines.

docs.t: What triggers the Parking Checklist?
docs.x: What triggers the Parking Checklist? Parking flow pattern completed Checklist trigger: After Parking flow pattern completed.

docs.t: Securing the Aircraft: who does it, and what kind of procedure is it?
docs.x: Securing the Aircraft: who does it, and what kind of procedure is it? PM. It is a Supplementary Procedure (FCOM PRO-NOR-SUP-SEC), read and do. Securing the Aircraft is performed by the PM and is a Supplementary Procedure. Refer to FCOM/PRO-NOR-SUP-SEC.

docs.t: Descent preparation: the FMS pages in FCOM order?
docs.x: Descent preparation: the FMS pages in FCOM order? ARRIVAL, F-PLN A, RADIO NAV, SELECTED NAVAIDS, DES WIND, PERF CRUISE, PERF DES, PERF APPR, PERF GO AROUND, FUEL PRED, PROG, SEC F-PLN. Then PM crosschecks. Then LDG ELEV and AUTO BRK. After the PF prepares the FMS, the PM checks all the data entered in the FMS. The PM should have the same mental image of the intended arrival and approach procedure, trajectory, and constraints than the PF.

docs.t: PERF APPR page: what goes in?
docs.x: PERF APPR page: what goes in? Guidance mode for a non-precision approach (FLS or FINAL APP), QNH, temperature and wind at destination, the minimum, the landing configuration (CONF FULL or CONF 3), the transition altitude/level ‐ Check or modify the landing configuration. Always select the landing configuration on the PERF APPR page:

docs.t: PERF APPR wind entry when the ATIS reads 15020G35KT?
docs.x: PERF APPR wind entry when the ATIS reads 15020G35KT? 150/20. Average wind only, never the gust. Ground Speed Mini handles the gust. Insert the average wind given by the ATC or ATIS. Do not insert the gust value.

docs.t: Autobrake mode for landing: how do you choose?
docs.x: Autobrake mode for landing: how do you choose? LO on long runways. MED on short or contaminated runways. MAX is not recommended at landing. Use of MAX mode is not recommended at landing. On short or contaminated runways, use MED mode. On long runways, LO mode is recommended

docs.t: Arrival Legs Verification: when, and who reads from what?
docs.x: Arrival Legs Verification: when, and who reads from what? After the FMGS descent preparation and before the Approach Briefing. PF reads from the ND (glass), PM verifies against the Jeppesen charts (paper). The Arrival Legs Verification will be accomplished after the FMGS descent preparation and before accomplishing the Approach Briefing.

docs.t: Approach Briefing: the Plan items on the Crew Briefing Card?
docs.x: Approach Briefing: the Plan items on the Crew Briefing Card? Route (STAR, Approach, Approach Mode); Missed Approach, Fuel/route to alternate; Landing Runway Assessment, Exit, Taxi; Autobrakes; Flaps, Approach/Target Speed. Threats first (PM, PF), Considerations after. • Route (STAR, Approach, Approach Mode)

docs.t: ILS: the three conditions before APPR pb, and what follows?
docs.x: ILS: the three conditions before APPR pb, and what follows? Cleared for the approach, on the intercept trajectory for the final approach course, LOC deviation available on the PFD. Then APPR pb press, BOTH APs engage (PF). - On the intercept trajectory for the final approach course - LOC deviation is available on the PFD - Cleared for Approach APPR pb…. Press

docs.t: Decelerated ILS: when is FLAPS 1 called, and when FLAPS 2?
docs.x: Decelerated ILS: when is FLAPS 1 called, and when FLAPS 2? FLAPS 1 at green dot, more than 3 NM before the FDP. FLAPS 2 at 2,500 ft AGL minimum. ‐ FLAPS 1 should be selected more than 3 NM before the Final Descent Point

docs.t: Go-around: the three simultaneous actions?
docs.x: Go-around: the three simultaneous actions? THRUST LEVERS TOGA, ROTATION toward 15 deg, announce GO AROUND (callout: GO AROUND - FLAPS) Simultaneously apply the following three actions:

docs.t: Go-around callouts in order, PF and PM?
docs.x: Go-around callouts in order, PF and PM? PF: GO AROUND - FLAPS. PM: FLAPS __. PM: POSITIVE CLIMB. PF: GEAR UP. PM: GEAR UP. GO AROUND decision GO AROUND - FLAPS Flaps retraction FLAPS__ Gear retraction POSITIVE CLIMB GEAR UP GEAR UP

docs.t: FMA after TOGA on the go-around?
docs.x: FMA after TOGA on the go-around? MAN TOGA / SRS / GA TRK or NAV / A/THR The following modes are displayed: MAN TOGA / SRS / GA TRK or NAV / A/THR.

docs.t: Why must the thrust levers touch TOGA even when TOGA thrust is not needed?
docs.x: Why must the thrust levers touch TOGA even when TOGA thrust is not needed? To engage the GO AROUND phase. Otherwise, within 7 NM of the airport the FMS sequences the destination waypoint. Set TOGA, then retard as required (CL keeps A/THR). If the thrust levers are not set briefly to TOGA detent, the FMS does not engage the GO AROUND phase, and flying over, or close to the airport (less than 7 NM) will sequence the Destination waypoint in the F-PLN.

docs.t: Go-around thrust reduction and acceleration altitudes: what happens at each?
docs.x: Go-around thrust reduction and acceleration altitudes: what happens at each? Thrust reduction: THRUST LEVERS CL when LVR CLB flashes (PF). Acceleration: monitor target speed increases to green dot; if not, check FCU ALT and pull the ALT knob. Then the Acceleration flow. Monitor that the target speed increases to Green Dot.

docs.t: Discontinued approach or go-around: which one, and when?
docs.x: Discontinued approach or go-around: which one, and when? At or above the FCU altitude: either the GO AROUND procedure or the discontinued approach (announce CANCEL APPROACH, press APPR or LOC pb to disarm, select modes and speed). Below the FCU altitude: GO AROUND procedure, mandatory. When the aircraft is below the FCU altitude, the flight crew must apply the GO AROUND procedure.

docs.t: Recite the A330 normal checklists in order
Who requests the checklist, who reads, who responds?
docs.x: Who requests the checklist, who reads, who responds? PF requests. PM reads the challenge (left side). PF responds after checking the actual aircraft status. The Pilot Flying (PF) requests the normal checklist.

docs.t: Which checklist follows Line-Up?
docs.x: Which checklist follows Line-Up? Approach. There is no after-takeoff or descent checklist on the A330. Checklist trigger: ‐ Below 10 000 ft AAL and barometric reference set, or

docs.t: What kind of checklist is an Airbus normal checklist?
docs.x: What kind of checklist is an Airbus normal checklist? Non-action. Every action is done from memory (the flow) first; the checklist only confirms. Airbus normal checklists are of a “non-action” type (i.e. all actions should be completed from memory before the flight crew performs the checklist).

docs.t: Checklist complete and checklist interrupted: the words?
docs.x: Checklist complete and checklist interrupted: the words? PM: __ CHECKLIST COMPLETE. If interrupted: HOLD CHECKLIST AT ___, then RESUME CHECKLIST AT ___. If a checklist needs to be interrupted, announce : “HOLD CHECKLIST AT ___” and “RESUME CHECKLIST AT ___” for the continuation. Upon completion of a checklist announce : “__CHECKLIST COMPLETE”.

docs.t: Landing Checklist when the LDG MEMO does not appear below 2,000 ft RA?
docs.x: Landing Checklist when the LDG MEMO does not appear below 2,000 ft RA? Use the expanded LDG MEMO section: LDG GEAR DN, SEAT BELTS ON, SPLRS ARM, FLAPS LDG. PM reads each challenge, PF responds each item. If the ECAM LDG MEMO does not annunciate below 2 000 ft RA, the expanded LDG MEMO section of the Landing Checklist is used by the flight crew. Once fully configured for landing, the PM must read the challenge and the PF must respond for each item.
